title: Step 67-D Admin login, FIDO and authenticated session lifecycle
description: HIGH-risk Admin frontend authentication stage. Implement username/password pre-auth entry, browser WebAuthn registration/authentication, server-only FIDO challenge/verify transport, authenticated session probing, fail-closed protected-route lifecycle, logout and neutral expired/revoked-session recovery. Preserve HttpOnly SameSite=Strict Admin/pre-auth cookie authority, never expose bearer/session tokens to browser JavaScript, never treat UI state as authorization, and defer permission-aware navigation, Step-Up UX, dashboard metrics and all domain administration to later stages.

dependencies.evidence: PR #354 merged; exact-SHA Canonical CI #1787, Phase A #1286 and CodeQL #934 SUCCESS; terminal Lock release comment 6144484040.

evidence.login_flow: POST /admin/auth/login -> pre-auth cookie -> POST /admin/auth/fido/challenge -> browser WebAuthn -> POST /admin/auth/fido/verify -> Admin session cookie
evidence.enrollment_flow: first credential requires server-validated enrollment_token; token is user-entered only and never persisted client-side

acceptance_criteria.description: A public /login route accepts username/password through a server action only. Browser JavaScript never receives pre_auth_token/session_token and credentials are not stored locally.

Successful login forwards only sanitized Backend Set-Cookie pre-auth evidence and transitions to a WebAuthn challenge state; invalid/rate-limited credentials fail closed with neutral Persian errors and no raw Backend error leakage.

FIDO challenge is requested server-side using only allow-listed pre-auth cookies. Authentication and initial-registration modes are distinguished only from authoritative response data; enrollment token is requested only when Backend returns the enrollment-required condition.

WebAuthn runs only through navigator.credentials in the browser using validated challenge options. Assertion/attestation serialization sends only the fields required by the existing Backend runtime and never stores credential material.

FIDO verification is proxied by a server action, captures only sanitized Admin Set-Cookie output, and on success enters the protected application without exposing session tokens to browser JavaScript.

Protected Admin routes probe GET /admin/auth/session on the server. Missing, expired, revoked or invalid sessions redirect/resolve to neutral unauthenticated recovery and never render protected content from stale browser state.
Authenticated root exposes only minimal server-proven staff identity type/id/accountId. Permissions/scopes, permission-aware navigation, Step-Up and dashboard runtime remain deferred.
Logout is server-only, forwards the authoritative Admin session cookie, captures the Backend clearing Set-Cookie, and returns to /login. Mutation requests are never automatically retried.

Deterministic Stage 67-D verification covers login/pre-auth cookie forwarding, WebAuthn encoding/serialization, authenticated/expired session route lifecycle, logout, Persian RTL/accessibility basics and stage-boundary exclusions.
No Backend/OpenAPI/generated-contract/database/Storefront/Product-Design/Current-State mutation is introduced; 67-E remains blocked.

HIGH-risk closure requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, CodeQL/Security, deterministic Review, exact-artifact ACTIVE Lock, Project Owner Human Gate, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Step 67-D is HIGH risk. Exact-artifact Project Owner approval is mandatory only after exact-head technical/security/review/Lock evidence is complete.
